reviews.justification: Arm B makes dispersed coverage directly auditable with a compact requirement-to-module ledger and defines a matched randomized protocol with explicit overhead limits; Arm A has a strong scheduling mechanism but a looser success condition and a greater risk that shallow first passes create rework.

Both interventions externalize edge contracts clearly, but Arm B enumerates concrete boundary dimensions and pairs them with held-out edge-focused scoring under controlled conditions; Arm A identifies more failure modes yet leaves acceptable cost increase undefined.

Arm B supplies an auditable risk ordering, a hard verification-budget cap, and explicit deadline-miss and overhead criteria, making efficiency easier to test. Arm A has the stronger adaptive counterexample mechanism and broader risk analysis, but selecting the most plausible violation and cheapest falsifier is less reproducible and its cost threshold is unspecified.
